module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1104

*Reference:* https://www.erdosproblems.com/1104
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos1104

open Filter SimpleGraph
open scoped Real

/-- Maximum chromatic number of a triangle-free graph on `n` vertices. -/
noncomputable def triangleFreeMaxChromatic (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {χ | ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 3 ∧ G.chromaticNumber = χ}

-- TODO: Add erdos_1104.

/--
Lower bound (Hefty–Horn–King–Pfender 2025).
$$
(1 - o(1)) \sqrt{\frac{n}{\log n}} \le f(n),
$$
where $f(n)$ denotes the maximum chromatic number of a triangle-free graph on
$n$ vertices, formalized as `triangleFreeMaxChromatic n`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1104.variants.lower :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (1 - ε) * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) / Real.sqrt (Real.log (n : ℝ))
        ≤ (triangleFreeMaxChromatic n : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Upper bound (Davies–Illingworth 2022).
$$
f(n) \le (2 + o(1)) \sqrt{\frac{n}{\log n}},
$$
where $f(n)$ denotes the maximum chromatic number of a triangle-free graph on
$n$ vertices, formalized as `triangleFreeMaxChromatic n`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1104.variants.upper :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (triangleFreeMaxChromatic n : ℝ)
        ≤ (2 + ε) * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) / Real.sqrt (Real.log (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1104

reformulations.difference: The source defines an attained maximum over n-vertex triangle-free graphs; Lean uses a natural-number supremum over graphs on Fin n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every n-vertex graph can be relabelled onto Fin n. Each chromatic number is finite and at most n, and the edgeless graph supplies a member of the defining set, including when n = 0. Thus the set is nonempty and bounded, and its natural-number supremum is its attained maximum. The scratch lemma maximum_spec proves triangleFreeMaxChromatic n = k iff k is the greatest element of this set.

reformulations.difference: Davies–Illingworth state the bound for every triangle-free n-vertex graph; Lean bounds their maximum chromatic number.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Bounding the attained maximum is equivalent to bounding every member of the family. The scratch lemma upper_graph_form proves the full equivalence to the explicit formulation: for every ε > 0, there exists N such that every triangle-free graph on Fin n, for every n ≥ N, has chromatic number at most (2 + ε)√(n/log n). It also verifies the square-root expression and eventual-quantifier translations.

sources_consulted: Zion Hefty, Paul Horn, Dylan King, Florian Pfender, Improving R(3,k) in just two bites, arXiv:2510.19718v3, introduction and Theorem 1.3. LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2510.19718v3 ; metadata: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.19718v3 .

Ewan Davies and Freddie Illingworth, The χ-Ramsey problem for triangle-free graphs, arXiv:2107.12288v2, §1, Theorem 1, and its proof. LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2107.12288v2 ; metadata: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.12288v2 .

review.notes: All three declarations were checked. Hefty–Horn–King–Pfender's independence-number bound gives the stated lower bound via χ(G) ≥ n/α(G); Davies–Illingworth explicitly prove the upper bound. Both research-solved tags are supported by these papers. Independent checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile successfully without using the admitted bounds. They establish the maximum specification, both graph-quantifier formulations, and values f(0)=0, f(1)=1, f(2)=2, alongside computable triangle-freeness tests. The logarithm/zero-division cases at n=0,1 do not affect eventual statements, and the denominator is positive for n≥2. Access limitation: https://www.erdosproblems.com/1104 repeatedly returned Cloudflare HTTP 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers. Its current commentary and metadata could not be checked directly; the declarations were verified against the primary papers instead.
